note: Labour (M20 C): the kingdom's hands and where they work through the seasons. A settlement's hands are a share of its people; villages within a day's walk by road lend theirs to the nearest town or city. The crown splits the hands by kind of work; each kind's hands spread over the matching works in proportion to what each needs. A works is staffed by the share of its need that is met.

fields.name: Fields
fields.note: Spring to the end of harvest. Idle from first frost.

woods.name: Woods and turf
woods.note: All year. Firewood, charcoal and peat matter most before winter.

pastures.name: Pastures
pastures.note: All year; most hands at the spring shearing.

fishing.name: Fishing
fishing.note: All year, but storms and ice close the water for weeks in winter.

repairs.name: Repairs
repairs.note: Masons and carpenters for the works being mended. Each crew is 160 hands.

levies.name: Levies
levies.note: Men under arms in the garrisons. More levies, fuller garrisons and emptier works.

need.note: Hands a works needs at full work, before placeScale. The farm need is the hands that work a place's own ground for its harvest, by kind of place.

fuel.note: Fuel in units that warm a hundred people for a winter month. Woods hands at a fuel works cut and dry it; elsewhere they gather what wood they can. Hearths burn it from November to March, most in midwinter.

harvest.name: Harvest muster
harvest.blurb: Everyone to the fields for six weeks: the harvest comes in faster and fuller; mines, crafts and repairs stall, and the people grumble.

winter.name: The winter turn
winter.blurb: At first frost the field hands go to the woods and the turf cuts, the boats and the workshops, until spring. A standing order.

levy.name: Raise the levies
levy.blurb: Hands become soldiers for three months: the garrisons fill and the realm is safer, but the works go short and the pay is dear.
